title: Maximum Area Rectangle With Point Constraints I
summary: Given an array of points, find the largest rectangle with sides parallel to the axes that includes exactly four points as vertices and no other points inside or on its edges.
statement: Given an array of points, find the largest rectangle with sides parallel to the axes that includes exactly four points as vertices and no other points inside or on its edges. Return the area if possible, otherwise return -1.
constraints: points contains 1–10 unique integer coordinates in 0..100.
A valid positive-area rectangle is axis-aligned, uses four listed corners, and contains no other listed point inside or on its border.
Return the largest valid area, or -1 when no rectangle exists.
hints: Opposite corners determine one axis-aligned rectangle and its other two required corners.
Enumerate point pairs, verify all four corners, then scan every point for forbidden occupancy.
Normalize x/y bounds; require the corner set and reject any non-corner within the closed rectangle.
Every rectangle has an opposite-corner pair, and the closed-region scan enforces both the interior and border restriction.
editorial: Every rectangle has an opposite-corner pair, and the closed-region scan enforces both the interior and border restriction.

The extra center point invalidates the only possible rectangle, so return -1.
